## Contributing Guidelines

Hi there! 👋 We're thrilled you want to help out with this project. To keep things running smoothly, please take a moment to review the guidelines below.

### How to Contribute

- **Fork the Repository.** Create a personal copy of the repository on your GitHub account.
- **Clone the Fork.** Download your forked repository to your local machine.
- **Create a New Branch.** For each new feature or fix, create a dedicated branch.
- **Make Changes.** Implement your changes on this new branch.
- **Add Tests.** Ensure your changes are covered by appropriate tests.
- **Commit Changes.** Commit your changes with a clear and descriptive message.
- **Push to GitHub.** Push your changes to your forked repository on GitHub.
- **Create a Pull Request.** Open a pull request from your forked repository to the main repository.

### Pull Request

Any contributions to this repository must be made through a pull request. Before submitting your pull request, please ensure the following:

- **Check for Existing Pull Requests.** Ensure there is no other pull request related to the same issue or feature request.
- **Update Documentation.** Update the README or any relevant documentation if necessary.
- **Reference Issues.** Reference the specific issue or feature request related to your pull request, if applicable.
- **Resolve Conflicts.** Ensure that your branch is up-to-date with the main branch and resolve any merge conflicts.

### Conventions

- **Branch Naming.** Use the format `version-task-or-issue#-username`. For example, `18.0-task#2983-johndoe`.
- **Commit Messages.** Follow the [Odoo Git Guidelines](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/18.0/contributing/development/git_guidelines.html) for formatting commit messages.
- **Coding Standards.** Use the [Odoo Coding Guidelines](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/18.0/contributing/development/coding_guidelines.html) to ensure consistency and quality across all contributions.

### Licence

This repository is licensed under [GNU General Public License v3.0](../LICENSE).

However, in some cases, a module may have a completely different license, so always check the license key in the module's __manifest__.py file for clarity.

Thanks for contributing! 🤝
